subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should maintainers accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92011 as a scoped embedded-runtime mitigation while this issue stays open for the remaining work-spawning surfaces, or require one cross-surface fix before landing any part?
rationale: Current main lacks the guard, but the viable open fix is deliberately partial and the remaining surfaces cross OpenClaw and Codex ownership boundaries.

options.title: Review Scoped PR, Keep Issue Open
options.body: Accept the linked PR only as an embedded sessions_spawn mitigation and keep this issue open until gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native follow-ups are owned.

options.title: Require Full Cross-Surface Fix
options.body: Pause the linked PR until one implementation covers every spawn-capable surface or explicitly removes unsupported surfaces from the invariant.

options.title: Split Remaining Surfaces Now
options.body: Create maintainer-owned follow-up issues for gateway loopback, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn_agent before deciding whether the scoped PR may land.

recommendation.title: Review Scoped PR, Keep Issue Open
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR only as an embedded sessions_spawn mitigation and keep this issue open until gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native follow-ups are owned.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned to the linked candidate PR and authored the cross-harness scope review that now blocks final issue resolution.
